Sought
sawt
v. (preterite and participle of seek; rendering Hebrew darash and baqash, Greek zeteo)
Preterite of seek, from the Saxon secan. Hebrew darash is to enquire of, to consult, and came to mean the diligent study of the law; baqash is to seek with desire, to search out. The English past tense preserves the sense of a search already made and answered.

Biblical Definition

Sought records seeking as an accomplished act, and Scripture is careful about what men seek and who seeks first. Of the believer it is the language of testimony: “I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears” (Psalm 34:4), and the Psalmist stakes his integrity on wholeness of pursuit, “With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments” (Psalm 119:10) — where even the man who has sought with his whole heart prays against wandering, which is honest about the residue of sin. But the decisive use reverses the direction. Isaiah records God saying, “I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not” (Isaiah 65:1) — a verse Paul applies to the calling of the Gentiles, and one of the clearest statements in the Old Testament that God takes the initiative in salvation. Men are found who were not looking. Ecclesiastes supplies the counterweight and diagnoses what unregenerate seeking actually pursues: “God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions” (Ecclesiastes 7:29). The faculty of seeking survived the fall; its direction did not.

Webster 1828 Definition

Preterite of seek. Believers testify that they sought the LORD and were heard; but Isaiah 65:1 reverses the direction — I am found of them that sought me not — and grace is prior.

expand to see more

SOUGHT, pret. and pp. of seek. [Sax. secan, to seek.] Went in search of; endeavored to find; solicited.

2. Asked for; requested; as, he sought counsel of the Lord.

3. Aimed at; endeavored to obtain; as, they sought his life.

4. Studied out; contrived; as, they have sought out many inventions, Eccl. 7.

5. In Scripture, I sought the Lord, and he heard me, Psa. 34; I am found of them that sought me not, Isa. 65.

Key Scripture

Psalm 34:4 — "I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears."

Psalm 119:10 — "With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments."

Isaiah 65:1 — "I am sought of them that asked not for me; I am found of them that sought me not: I said, Behold me, behold me, unto a nation that was not called by my name."

Ecclesiastes 7:29 — "Lo, this only have I found, that God hath made man upright; but they have sought out many inventions."

Modern Corruption

The spiritual search is now spoken of as the seeker's achievement, and church programmes are built round the seeker. Scripture says the natural man seeks out inventions, and that God is found of those who were not seeking him.

expand to see more

Seeker-centred ministry rests on an anthropology Scripture does not grant. Romans states flatly that there is none that seeketh after God, and Ecclesiastes 7:29 explains what the search faculty produces when left to itself — many inventions, the endless manufacture of religion. That is not a denial that men are religious; it is an account of why their religion never arrives. The seeking that finds God is itself the fruit of grace already at work, which is why Isaiah 65:1 can put the discovery before the search.

The correction must not be pressed into fatalism. Psalm 34:4 and Psalm 119:10 are genuine testimonies of genuine seeking, and Scripture everywhere commands men to seek the LORD while he may be found. Both are true because effectual calling does not bypass the will but renews it: God seeks first, and the man he has sought then seeks him, and seeks him with his whole heart. The principle to recover is the order. Where the order is reversed, assurance rests on the strength of one's own pursuit, which is a poor foundation on a bad day.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew darash is to enquire of or consult, later to study the law; baqash is to seek with desire. Greek zeteo is to seek and ekzeteo to seek out diligently, the word of Hebrews 11:6.

expand to see more

Hebrew darash (H1875) — to enquire, to consult, to seek diligently; the root of later Jewish midrash.

Hebrew baqash (H1245) — to seek, to search out, to desire; used of seeking God's face.

Greek zeteo (G2212) — to seek; seek ye first the kingdom of God.

Greek ekzeteo (G1567) — to seek out earnestly; God is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him.

Greek epizeteo (G1934) — to seek after, to crave; used of what the Gentiles seek after.

Usage

"Of answered seeking: I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears (Psalm 34:4)."

"Of grace preceding the search: I am found of them that sought me not (Isaiah 65:1)."

"Of what fallen men actually seek: they have sought out many inventions (Ecclesiastes 7:29)."
